entities.summary: A compact sea-to-summit island ascent above the outer Sunnfjord archipelago, with enormous Atlantic sightlines.
entities.description:
Start at the Aldenvågen visitor landing approach and follow the established signed approach up to the farm. Continue on the existing narrow, steep path to the plateau, then visit the eastern Instenova walking ground. Return to the plateau junction and take the existing western path to the Ystenova crest for the sea and island views. Retrace the paths and farm approach to the same landing. Approximate planning totals are 5.9 km, 480 m ascent and descent, and 3 hours 30 minutes. Distance is calculated from the complete mapped line; climbing and time totals are approximate planning estimates without a surveyed elevation profile.

Choose suitable dry, snow-free daylight and allow extra time for conditions. The approach has signs, but the visible mountain paths are unmarked; do not expect continuous waymarks. Narrow steep sections, loose stones, summit drops and coastal wind require careful footing. Stay back from exposed summit and cliff margins, and avoid strong wind, rain, snow or ice. Stay on the established signed farm approach and existing paths, respect landowner instructions, livestock and current closures, and avoid farmyards or private ground outside that approach. Confirm outward and return boat transport and the current landing terms separately; neither boat service nor landing availability is guaranteed. If any required ground is closed, prohibited or unsafe, this complete itinerary is unavailable.

entities.summary: A remote plateau hike from Jordalen to a huge viewpoint directly above the UNESCO-listed Nærøyfjord.
entities.description:
Start by Jordalen’s community house, follow the established road and Slettedalen walking path past the summer farms, and continue through the upper valley and Lyngsskaret mountain area to the original main Bakkanosi summit ground. Return along the same normal walking course. The complete mapped return is approximately 16.8 km; the inherited climbing and time figures remain approximate planning estimates.

Choose suitable snow-free July–September daylight and allow extra time for conditions. The mountain route is unmarked and sometimes indistinct; bring a proper map and compass. Fog, boggy ground, lingering snow and dangerous snow cornices near the fjord rim require care. Stay back from the exposed rim and do not follow stray snow footprints away from the normal path. Use the signed paid landowner parking and keep roads clear for farmers and emergency vehicles. Respect farms, livestock, wild reindeer and current local instructions; keep dogs leashed. Fill water before the hike, as water can be limited. If any required ground is closed, prohibited or unsafe, the complete itinerary is unavailable.

Route geometry: © OpenStreetMap contributors; identifiable GPS trace Bakkanosi_Trail.gpx by Nik-O-Dim — https://www.openstreetmap.org/user/Nik-O-Dim/traces/2275880. ODbL 1.0 — https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/. Changes: selected the complete original normal trail to the main Bakkanosi summit ground, added the existing Jordalen road approach through an exact source-segment intersection, and retraced the full walking course. Original339-point provider collection is retained; source continuation beyond the original main-summit purpose is excluded. No synthetic connector, private operator/author GPX geometry or elevation profile. Planning only; not navigation-grade.
entities.whyWorthwhile: It combines world-class fjord scale with a serious uncrowded mountain day and avoids the queue-and-photo-stop character of Norway's best-known cliff viewpoints.

entities.summary: A historic railway-construction road descending through waterfalls, tunnels and abandoned infrastructure to roadless Rombaksbotn.
entities.description:
Walk the full Riksgränsen crossing from the Riksgränsvägen–Rallarvägen walking junction to the Rombaksbotn pier approach: approximately 17.2 km and about six hours. Bjørnfjell is a practical shorter start, not this default course. Approximate terrain-derived ascent is 270 m and descent 780 m, with uncertainty around 100 m or more. The historical terrain source dates to 2013, with a January 2018 tile-feed update; foreign-side terrain quality is uncertain. Ground modelling, including at bridges and tunnels, is not an operator measurement, field survey or walking elevation profile. Prepare for cold, fog, wind, snow or ice and wet rough ground on this high-country historic road. Check local conditions and obey restrictions; source capture is not an all-open guarantee. Recorded bridges/tunnel, two fords and a lift gate require careful assessment on the ground; water levels and gate conditions are not established by mapping. Cross the railway only at the designated walking crossing, heed trains and signals, and never walk on railway tracks. Arrange and confirm the roadless Rombaksbotn return before departure. Published July–mid-September boat/bus arrangements do not establish October service. OSM source edits span 2012–2026. The planning line is not a field inspection or navigation-grade track.

entities.summary: A three-to-four-day hut circuit through Trollheimen's unusually varied valleys, lakes, birch woodland and high passes.
entities.description:
Walk the complete three-to-four-day triangle from Gjevilvasshytta to Jøldalshytta, then over Geithøtta to Trollheimshytta, returning through Riarskaret and Mellomfjellet to Gjevilvasshytta. The first leg follows the hut road and birch-woodland path past Høghøa, across Minilla and over Skrikhøa. The second follows Gammelseterdalen, crosses Litlsvartåa and climbs Geithøtta before descending beside Slettåa. The final leg climbs through Skallen and Mellomfjellet, passes Fossådalsvatnet, crosses Riarskaret and follows the eastern side of Kamtjønnin and the foot of Blåhøa before Gravbekken and the hut road. Do not substitute the more demanding Trollhetta summit traverse or a different second-leg itinerary. The complete triangle has three consecutive walking stages divided at Jøldalshytta and Trollheimshytta.

Choose dry, snow-free summer conditions for this demanding, remote mountain circuit. Long days, steep rocky paths, boggy ground, exposed high passes, rapidly changing weather and cumulative fatigue require suitable footwear, warm and waterproof clothing, map and compass, food, drink and adequate daylight. The responsible guide grades the Riars leg VERY_TOUGH. Turn back or postpone if weather, visibility, footing or any required crossing is unsafe. Verify current local signs, lawful restrictions, path and bridge conditions before departure; the entire itinerary is unavailable if a required leg or bridge is closed, prohibited or unsafe. Gravbekken bridge has its rails removed in winter: this is not a winter route. Mapped markings and retained guide accounts do not promise that every marker or crossing is usable today.

Walk considerately on the established paths through Trollheimen's protected landscape and Svartåmoen reserve. Avoid vegetation damage, wildlife disturbance, litter and shortcuts. This ordinary self-guided walking recommendation grants no permission for organised events, trail marking, maintenance, construction or motor access. Confirm hut accommodation, bookings and seasonal services separately from walking access; a hut's booking or opening status alone does not establish whether a trail is open.

The complete mapped course is approximately 58.5 km. The retained 1,490 m ascent, 1,490 m descent and 1,260 minutes of walking are approximate legacy planning estimates for a three-to-four-day itinerary, not surveyed heights, a measured elevation profile or a time guarantee. No elevations are assigned to this route.

variants.name: Gjevilvasshytta–Jøldalshytta–Geithøtta–Trollheimshytta–Riarskaret summer triangle
variants.description:
Walk the complete three-to-four-day triangle from Gjevilvasshytta to Jøldalshytta, then over Geithøtta to Trollheimshytta, returning through Riarskaret and Mellomfjellet to Gjevilvasshytta. The first leg follows the hut road and birch-woodland path past Høghøa, across Minilla and over Skrikhøa. The second follows Gammelseterdalen, crosses Litlsvartåa and climbs Geithøtta before descending beside Slettåa. The final leg climbs through Skallen and Mellomfjellet, passes Fossådalsvatnet, crosses Riarskaret and follows the eastern side of Kamtjønnin and the foot of Blåhøa before Gravbekken and the hut road. Do not substitute the more demanding Trollhetta summit traverse or a different second-leg itinerary. The complete triangle has three consecutive walking stages divided at Jøldalshytta and Trollheimshytta.

Choose dry, snow-free summer conditions for this demanding, remote mountain circuit. Long days, steep rocky paths, boggy ground, exposed high passes, rapidly changing weather and cumulative fatigue require suitable footwear, warm and waterproof clothing, map and compass, food, drink and adequate daylight. The responsible guide grades the Riars leg VERY_TOUGH. Turn back or postpone if weather, visibility, footing or any required crossing is unsafe. Verify current local signs, lawful restrictions, path and bridge conditions before departure; the entire itinerary is unavailable if a required leg or bridge is closed, prohibited or unsafe. Gravbekken bridge has its rails removed in winter: this is not a winter route. Mapped markings and retained guide accounts do not promise that every marker or crossing is usable today.

Walk considerately on the established paths through Trollheimen's protected landscape and Svartåmoen reserve. Avoid vegetation damage, wildlife disturbance, litter and shortcuts. This ordinary self-guided walking recommendation grants no permission for organised events, trail marking, maintenance, construction or motor access. Confirm hut accommodation, bookings and seasonal services separately from walking access; a hut's booking or opening status alone does not establish whether a trail is open.

The complete mapped course is approximately 58.5 km. The retained 1,490 m ascent, 1,490 m descent and 1,260 minutes of walking are approximate legacy planning estimates for a three-to-four-day itinerary, not surveyed heights, a measured elevation profile or a time guarantee. No elevations are assigned to this route.

entities.summary: A long linear path following the Gaula water system past numerous waterfalls, lakes and old summer farms.
entities.description:
Follow the complete marked Fossestien walking main from the Gaularfjellet/Torsnesstølen source walking entry down the Gaula water and cultural landscape through the Longestølen and Likholefossen phases to its adopted western river-path finish at Eldal in Viksdalen. The original day-long purpose is the full linear walk, with return transport arranged. Follow the red F marks, arrows and named signs through forest paths, wooden bridges and footbridges, old summer-pasture grounds and the narrow lower gorge. The four named parking/map places offer alternative starts; this full course does not add dead-end parking excursions, relocate to a representative farm centroid or extend along a road to a shuttle pickup.

Select dry, snow-free June–October walking conditions with sufficient daylight and check current maintenance and weather before departure. Expect wet or muddy footing, slippery wooden bridges, narrow river/gorge passages and increased water hazards after heavy rain. Use sturdy footwear and follow maintained walking ground; no cycling or riding. Close gates, keep dogs leashed as requested and respect active farms and livestock. In Sunnfjord, the local grazing-related leash rule is conditional from 1 April to 1 November; residential and other applicable rules remain separate, and that local regulation is not generalized to Sogndal. Ordinary careful walking is subject to current Friluftsloven and actual local signs. The protected-area query found no polygons, which does not grant blanket private-property or river access. If any required walking leg is closed, prohibited or unsafe, the whole itinerary is unavailable.

Arrange point-to-point return transport in advance. Hov Hyttegrend offers a paid shuttle which must be booked no later than the previous day; verify current availability and pickup arrangements. Neither endpoint parking nor a connecting road walk is guaranteed or included.

The complete selected course is approximately 18.8 km from every original source edge, correcting the earlier marketed 21 km estimate after full named-course review. Approximate 540 m ascent and 920 m descent are historical 10 m terrain/API estimates, using bilinear samples on the complete route and centred 25 m sample-mean smoothing, rounded to 10 m. Smoothing sensitivity is substantial: 50 m smoothing gives about 450 m ascent / 830 m descent, and 100 m gives about 360 m / 750 m — roughly 90–180 m variation around the 25 m estimate. Terrain age, local error and density-weighted sampling add uncertainty. These are planning estimates, not field/GPS measurements, direct publisher measurements or a precise current elevation profile. No point heights or vertical datum are claimed. The earlier 220 m ascent and the publisher’s 500 m altitude difference are not used as total-descent estimates. Inherited 420 minutes remains an approximate planning duration; allow additional time for footing, weather and stops.

entities.summary: A little-known hike to a dramatic glacial-outburst gorge often described as Rogaland's Jutulhogget.
entities.description:
From the Vinddalen hut and parking walking approach, follow the red T-marked Driftaveien through Fårelia and the steep Ytre Fåreliskaret ascent. Pass the pond, continue through Sletteskaret and descend past small ponds and wet ground to the first upper-inner Fossjuvet gorge viewpoint. Return along exactly the same path to Vinddalen. The farther bridge and fallhead visit are optional extensions outside this selected route. The complete course is approximately 10.2 km.

Loose gravel, sand and stones on steep Ytre Fåreliskaret are slippery, especially on descent; wet bog, streams and rock require care.

The upper-inner-gorge rim is exposed and unfenced: keep well back, particularly in wind or wet conditions. Prefer dry, snow-free May–October daylight subject to actual conditions.

Follow current signs, lawful restrictions and closures, and travel carefully in Frafjordheiane without harming vegetation, wildlife or cultural remains. The whole outback is unavailable if any required leg is prohibited, closed or unsafe.

Return from the first upper-inner gorge viewpoint. The farther bridge/fallhead extension and exposed Røssdalen circuit are excluded; no current bridge condition or current sign presence is asserted.

Allow about 4–6 hours plus stops for the whole course; inherited 628 m ascent and descent are approximate planning estimates without a measured elevation profile.

entities.summary: A granite-dome hike above the great lake Nisser, with unusually open slab terrain and broad inland panoramas.
entities.description:
From the Landtakdammen parking area, use its existing walking access onto Borstadvegen, then follow the ordinary mountain paths to the main Hægefjell summit walking ground. Return to the same parking ingress by the exact same course. This recommendation is for the established hiking approach, not any climbing route, an extended loop or a visit to the mountain's slab margins.

Choose dry, snow-free conditions. Granite slabs can become very slippery when wet or icy; fog and poor visibility make the open upper terrain difficult to follow. Stay well back from slab margins and summit drops. Wear suitable footwear and carry map and compass, warm and waterproof clothing, food, drink and enough daylight. Turn back if weather, visibility, footing or navigation becomes uncertain. Confirm current road and parking access, local signs, trail conditions and lawful restrictions before departure; the whole itinerary is unavailable if a required leg is closed, prohibited or unsafe. Walk considerately on the established paths, avoid vegetation damage, wildlife disturbance, litter and shortcuts. No climbing or camping permission is implied.

Waymarking is partial: some mountain approach sections are mapped as marked, while continuous marking on the upper footpath and summit approach is not confirmed. Do not rely on the map or markings alone. The source is descriptive community mapping, not a current field survey or a guarantee of safe or open ground.

The complete mapped return is approximately 8.8 km. From the Landtakdammen parking area, use its existing walking access onto Borstadvegen, then follow the ordinary mountain paths to the main Hægefjell summit walking ground. Stay well back from slab margins and summit drops. Wear suitable footwear and carry map and compass, warm and waterproof clothing, food, drink and enough daylight. Turn back if weather, visibility, footing or navigation becomes uncertain. Confirm current road and parking access, local signs, trail conditions and lawful restrictions before departure; the whole itinerary is unavailable if a required leg is closed, prohibited or unsafe. entities.summary: A long, quiet Arctic crossing to the monumental Kjøttvikvarden and a roughly 300 m Barents Sea cliff on northern Sørøya.
entities.description:
From the Akkarfjord boat landing on Sørøya, follow the waterfront service road and the road toward Gamvik, then Petterveien and the marked/local mountain path to the ordinary standing and viewing ground beside Kjøttvikvarden. Return by the same complete course to the boat landing. Stay well back from the sea cliffs; this hike does not continue along the cliff edge or coast. The cairn is protected heritage: do not climb, damage or tamper with it.

Allow about seven hours for this demanding, remote outing, with additional time for rests and conditions. The complete mapped return is approximately 15.9 km. The retained 525 m ascent and descent are approximate legacy planning estimates, not surveyed heights or an elevation profile. Rough and boggy ground, wind, fog, cold and limited infrastructure require suitable footwear, map and compass, food, drink and enough daylight. Choose dry, snow-free conditions; turn back if visibility, weather, ground or navigation becomes uncertain. Verify current local signs, access restrictions, closures and markings, walk considerately and avoid disturbing wildlife or property access.

Waymarking is partial and must be checked locally. The current guide describes a T-marked approach, while the mapped upper path contains resurvey and marking-check notes and includes tracing from Strava heatmaps. The coarse guide and mapped path differ locally by about 112 m on the upper approach. This descriptive map is not a current field survey, marking confirmation or safety guarantee.

Arrange and confirm current boat access and the return before departure. The official B380 timetable valid October 2026–May 2027 marks Akkarfjord calls as requiring advance request. Check current operator arrangements and disruptions; this map promises no departure, availability or boat service.

entities.summary: A low coastal walk across enormous glacial-moraine boulder beaches facing the Skagerrak.
entities.description:
Start at the Mølen visitor parking and follow the existing footpaths west into the main southern moraine walking grounds. Continue on the field path and gravel track, take the pebblestone footpath to its end and return along the same short spur. Follow the coastal Kyststien leg and the other existing eastern coastal path back to the same parking. The loop combines main moraine and boulder-beach walking grounds with the coastal landscape.

Waymarking is partial; continuous signing of every footpath and the pebblestone spur is not confirmed. Use suitable footwear and a map, and watch for vehicles around the parking access. Rounded loose stones can roll underfoot, and wet or icy rock is slippery. Choose snow-free ground and calm weather, keep clear of breaking waves, and avoid this exposed coast during storms or strong winds. Turn back if footing, weather, visibility or navigation is uncertain.

Leave all stones and cultural remains in place. Do not climb burial cairns, remove stones, build new cairns or dig sun holes. Avoid disturbing birds and vegetation, take litter away, walk considerately on the established grounds and follow current dog controls. Check current local signs, lawful restrictions, path conditions and closures before departure. If any required moraine, pebblestone or coastal leg is closed, prohibited or unsafe, the whole selected itinerary is unavailable.

The complete mapped loop is approximately 1.6 km. The inherited 90 m ascent, 90 m descent and 195 minutes remain approximate historical planning estimates, not surveyed elevations, a measured height profile or a time guarantee. No elevations are assigned. Community mapping is descriptive planning information, not a current field survey or a guarantee that the ground is safe or open.

variants.name: Mølen main moraine, pebblestone and coastal loop
variants.description:
Start at the Mølen visitor parking and follow the existing footpaths west into the main southern moraine walking grounds. Continue on the field path and gravel track, take the pebblestone footpath to its end and return along the same short spur. Follow the coastal Kyststien leg and the other existing eastern coastal path back to the same parking. The loop combines main moraine and boulder-beach walking grounds with the coastal landscape.

Waymarking is partial; continuous signing of every footpath and the pebblestone spur is not confirmed. Use suitable footwear and a map, and watch for vehicles around the parking access. Rounded loose stones can roll underfoot, and wet or icy rock is slippery. Choose snow-free ground and calm weather, keep clear of breaking waves, and avoid this exposed coast during storms or strong winds. Turn back if footing, weather, visibility or navigation is uncertain.

Leave all stones and cultural remains in place. Do not climb burial cairns, remove stones, build new cairns or dig sun holes. Avoid disturbing birds and vegetation, take litter away, walk considerately on the established grounds and follow current dog controls. Check current local signs, lawful restrictions, path conditions and closures before departure. If any required moraine, pebblestone or coastal leg is closed, prohibited or unsafe, the whole selected itinerary is unavailable.

The complete mapped loop is approximately 1.6 km. The inherited 90 m ascent, 90 m descent and 195 minutes remain approximate historical planning estimates, not surveyed elevations, a measured height profile or a time guarantee. entities.summary: An Atlantic island circuit combining open moor, historic lighthouse and Runde's great seabird cliffs.
entities.description:
From the walking aisle inside Goksøyr parking, follow Goksøyrvegen to the signed climb onto the plateau. Take the existing cliff approach and complete stair spur to the Lundeura viewpoint, return to the path, and visit Rundebranden before continuing along the western cliff. Descend the established spur to the lower Runde lighthouse visitor courtyard and return on that shared lower path. Use the eastern walking path and northern boardwalk/plateau route back to the same Goksøyr parking ground. This complete loop is approximately 8.5 km; inherited planning estimates are 560 m ascent, 560 m descent and 3 hours 30 minutes. They are approximate and do not represent a surveyed elevation profile; allow extra time for conditions.

Recommend a dry, snow-free September visit for the complete circuit. In Runde bird-protection areas 1–3, travel is prohibited from March 15 through August 31 except on explicitly marked paths to and from explicitly marked viewpoints. That exception has not been established for this full western-cliff circuit. During that period use this whole itinerary only if current official local markings and instructions expressly permit every required protected leg; otherwise the complete itinerary is unavailable. Do not omit Lundeura or the western cliff to create a replacement. Current protected boundaries, signs and closures also govern outside those dates.

Keep to existing paths, paved steps and boardwalks. Protect vegetation, birds, nests and young; obey current local signs, bird-protection boundaries, landowner instructions and closures. Unprotected cliffs, strong coastal wind, slippery or muddy ground, steep lighthouse descent and viewpoint stairs require dry snow-free daylight, suitable footwear and careful footing. The Goksøyr road approach carries ordinary traffic, including a mapped 80 km/h segment; continuous protected pavement is not established. entities.description:

This original self-guided point-to-point itinerary finishes at the parking boundary; optional museum or Vemork bridge visits require separate arrangements. The complete mapped course is approximately 6.6 km. Inherited estimates of 245 m ascent, 526 m descent and 180 minutes are approximate planning figures, not surveyed heights or a measured elevation profile. The original guide allows 3–5 hours; allow extra time for weather and history stops.

Major traffic exposure: approximately 730 m of walking on a mapped 80 km/h section of FV37, then 170 m on a 50 km/h road, plus ordinary Våer street traffic. These are walking intervals, not just short crossings. A continuous separated pavement, usable shoulder or protected crossing has not been established. Use a walking path, pavement or shoulder where available; where carriageway walking is permitted, follow current Norwegian pedestrian rules, normally the extreme left edge unless the opposite side is safer. Use nearby designated crossings where available and cross only without danger or undue traffic disturbance. Obey actual signs, roadworks and closures. Do not attempt a required road passage if traffic, weather or visibility makes it unsafe.

entities.summary: A short but brutally steep Hjørundfjord summit with vast views over fjord arms and Sunnmøre's sharp peaks.
entities.description:
From the Kvistadsætra walking parking, follow the southward gravel and tractor road to the Skårasalen turn, then the intermittent path up the left side of the rocky gully. Continue north toward the passage between Blåhornet and Skårasalen, across the upper plateau toward the Lille Skårasalen saddle, then climb the scree to the main Skårasalen summit. Return by the same normal course. The direct ascent across the central slope and any minor summit or optional cliff viewpoint are outside this selected hike. Retain the original approximate planning figures: 6.8 km, 1,030 m ascent and descent, and five hours; they are not a surveyed elevation profile.

Use this expert route only in dry, snow-free conditions. Very steep ground, loose upper scree and consequential terrain require care; turn back if conditions or the upper terrain feel consequential. Do not continue over snow, ice or wet rock. Verify current signs, access and conditions before walking. The principal N50 path is a historic digitized record captured in 2007 with stated 20 m accuracy, no marking recorded, and an unknown update date represented by the source placeholder 1000-01-01. The current summer guide describes an indistinct, intermittent path; the map is not a current field survey or an all-open guarantee. A report published on 10 July 2026 described snow blocking the normal trail on that trip; this is a historical observation, not current closure or safe-snow advice. Walk considerately and respect current local restrictions and property access.

entities.description:
Follow the Skeisnesset geological coastal loop from the existing road departure down to Våttviksletta. Continue along the shoreline rocks around Våttvikodden and north to Vardvika, then take the coastal continuation to Bukkatalgen and return inland on the existing tractor-road and family-path connections to the same departure. The route visits Leka’s distinctive ancient-ocean-crust and coastal rock landscape.

Waymarking is partial. The Vardvika–Bukkatalgen cliff-side continuation is explicitly unmarked; signage is also incomplete on the geological and inland family-path grounds. Use suitable footwear, map and compass, and allow ample time and daylight for rough coastal rock. Choose snow-free ground and calm conditions: exposed wind, wet or icy rock, poor visibility and waves can make the shoreline and cliff-side ground unsafe. Stay well back from cliff edges and breaking waves, avoid shortcuts and turn back if footing, weather or navigation is uncertain.

Check current local signs, lawful restrictions, path conditions and closures before departure. If any required coastal or return segment is closed, prohibited or unsafe, the whole selected itinerary is unavailable. Walk considerately on the established grounds, avoid courtyards and unreasonable disturbance to residents, livestock, vegetation and wildlife; leave burial mounds and other cultural remains undisturbed and take all litter away. Follow current dog controls. The map is descriptive planning information, not a current field survey or a guarantee that the route is safe or open.

The complete mapped loop is approximately 2.1 km. The inherited 80 m ascent, 80 m descent and 195 minutes remain approximate historical planning estimates, not surveyed elevations, a measured height profile or a time guarantee. No elevations are assigned. The released mapping retains source captures from 2004 and 2020 and updates from 2023, with original geometry-origin and quality annotations preserved privately; it is not a new ground survey.

warnings: The operator gives May–October and 1.5–2.5 hours; frost, rain and darkness make steep stonework harder.
Use Svartegjel parking rather than the stave-church visitor centre for a walking visit; a Rimskjold start is also expressly supported.
